first_check.explanation: The Georgia Trade Secrets Act is real and provides a misappropriation claim. However, the Act begins at § 10-1-760 (Short Title), and Georgia courts cite it as 'OCGA § 10-1-760 et seq.' Section 10-1-761 is the Definitions section. Starting the et seq. cite at 761 still covers the operative provisions (761 definitions through 767), so this is a small citation defect, not a wrong authority.

first_check.correct_citation: Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, Inc., 509 U.S. 579 (1993)
first_check.explanation: The budget uses 'Daubert' only as the common name for a motion to exclude expert testimony, not as a cite for a holding. Daubert is the Supreme Court case setting the standard for admitting expert scientific testimony, so describing expert-exclusion motions as 'Daubert motions' is accurate. The matter is in Georgia state court (Fulton County Superior Court). The Georgia Supreme Court cites Daubert in its expert-admissibility decisions (e.g., Miller v. Golden Peanut Co., 317 Ga. 22 (2023); Monroe v. State, 313 Ga. 458 (2022)), so the label fits there too.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: 509 U.S. 579 (1993) ... In this case we are called upon to determine the standard for admitting expert scientific testimony in a federal trial.

first_check.correct_citation: O.C.G.A. § 10-1-760 et seq. (Georgia Trade Secrets Act); misappropriation is defined at § 10-1-761(2)
first_check.explanation: Section 10-1-761 is the Act's Definitions section, which defines 'trade secret' and 'misappropriation' (§ 10-1-761(2)). The remedies for a claim are in §§ 10-1-762 (injunctive relief) and 10-1-763 (damages). Calling these 'claims under § 10-1-761' is an imprecise shorthand for claims under the whole Act, though the provision is closely tied to the elements of the claim. It is a minor citation defect only. The cite is used for an attorney's experience, which is not a legal proposition.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: § 10-1-761 - Definitions; § 10-1-762 - Injunctive Relief; § 10-1-763 - Recovery of Damages; O.C.G.A. 10-1-761(2), 'Misappropriation' means: (A) Acquisition of a trade secret of another by a person who knows or has reason to know that the trade secret was acquired by improper means...
